 Editorials Why the Lakers could turn to Kevon Looney against the Hornets
 Last updated: November 17, 2026 2:14 pm 
 Lakers Daily 
 Share 
 7 Min Read 
 Kevon Looney played the final 4:25 against the Milwaukee Bucks last week. With Walker Kessler out against the Charlotte Hornets on Tuesday, JJ Redick has a reason to call his number considerably earlier.
 Charlotte’s two centers combined for eight offensive rebounds Sunday against the Los Angeles Clippers. Kessler pulled down six offensive boards himself that afternoon in Phoenix.
 Now the Los Angeles Lakers have to contend with Moussa Diabate and Ryan Kalkbrenner without the player who did the most to earn them extra shots against the Suns. The NBA’s Tuesday injury report lists Kessler out with right lower leg soreness and Austin Reaves out with a bruised left heel.
 In his pregame breakdown of Lakers-Hornets, Jovan Buha raised Looney as one option for Kessler’s first missed game of the season. Buha also laid out the alternatives.
 Sandro Mamukelashvili gives Luka Doncic room to operate with five Lakers outside the paint. Jarred Vanderbilt gives Redick a mobile defender who can fight for rebounds.
 Looney’s opportunity could come when Charlotte goes to its bench, even if Redick prefers one of the other two alongside Doncic at tipoff.
 Tonight is a big test for the Lakers defensively without Walker Kessler, especially on the glass. Hornets rank 3rd in OREB%, 1st in DREB%, and 2nd in REB%. pic.twitter.com/dD9sFhjU2P 
 — Jovan Buha (@jovanbuha) November 17, 2026 
 Charlotte’s backup center gives the Lakers a reason to use Looney
 Diabate grabbed five offensive rebounds in just over 26 minutes against the Clippers. Getting him off the floor brought little relief.
 Kalkbrenner picked up three more in 18:20 off the bench. The Hornets finished with 17 offensive rebounds to the Clippers’ five.
 Charlotte shot 38 percent and still attempted 18 more field goals than the team that beat it. That game offers Redick a useful distinction.
 The Lakers can get the initial matchup right, force a difficult shot and still give away the possession if their center is the player who had to challenge it.
 Charlotte attempted 52 shots from beyond the arc against the Clippers. On those misses, there is work for the Lakers’ perimeter players as well.
 Whoever is closest to Diabate has to find him while the shot is in the air, particularly if the center has followed the ball away from the rim.
 Buha put Charlotte third in the NBA in offensive rebound percentage and first in defensive rebound percentage entering Tuesday. The latter ranking matters for Looney, too.
 If he can make Charlotte send a second player to box him out, a Lakers miss gives the Hornets one fewer player free to take off up the floor. Few of the Lakers’ reserve options have made a living doing exactly that.
 Asked about his rebounding after Golden State eliminated Sacramento in Game 7 of their 2023 playoff series, Looney said, “I just wanted to get us extra possessions, set the tone with physicality and energy.”
 He had seven offensive boards in the third quarter alone. It has been more than three years since that game, and his recent assignment with the Lakers has been considerably smaller.
 The official Milwaukee game book credits him with one rebound at each end in his four-plus minutes. A short shift opposite Kalkbrenner would give him a specific job after another stretch of limited minutes.
 What Redick loses if he moves Mamukelashvili to center
 Starting Mamukelashvili would give the Lakers a way to make Diabate work farther from the basket. If he follows Mamukelashvili above the arc, Doncic has one fewer defender waiting on a drive.
 If he stays home, Doncic has a passing option behind the play. With Reaves sidelined, creating that choice for the defense has added value. The trade-off shows up when Redick goes to his second unit.
 Against Phoenix, Redick opened both the second and fourth quarters with Mamukelashvili and Kessler together. Doncic was on the bench to start both periods.
 In those groups, Mamukelashvili could play away from the rim and Kessler could pursue a miss. Four of Kessler’s six offensive rebounds came in the second quarter.
 Using Mamukelashvili exclusively at center would take that arrangement away from a unit already missing Reaves. Redick has tried another version with Vanderbilt.
 In October, when Vanderbilt moved into the rotation against the Clippers , he drew the Brook Lopez assignment and collected seven rebounds. Mamukelashvili supplied 13 points, eight rebounds and three assists.
 Vanderbilt could spend a possession denying an entry pass to Lopez knowing the Lakers still had another big on the floor. On the next trip, Mamukelashvili could step outside and leave the lane open for Vanderbilt to cut.
 There is a case for giving that pairing the first opportunity against Charlotte. Redick has already seen it work, and it addresses a concern he raised in the preseason.
 In discussing how he wanted the Lakers to rebound without Kessler , Redick identified Doncic, Adou Thiero and Mamukelashvili as examples of bigger players he could put on the wings. One advantage to using Looney for a shift is that it frees Redick to use Mamukelashvili in precisely that role.
 The telling substitution Tuesday could come when Diabate takes his first rest. If Vanderbilt and the wings can keep Kalkbrenner off the offensive glass, Redick can keep an extra shooter or ballhandler alongside Doncic.
 If Charlotte’s second unit starts collecting its own misses, Looney can change that matchup without Redick having to undo his starting lineup. For a veteran who got four minutes in Milwaukee, that first-half call would say more about his place in this game than whose name gets announced before tipoff.
